After the deluge

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After the recent floods - Toyota was under water - what its taken to get back up and running

Unique Selling Point:
Footage of the flooding inside the plant, the inside story of what it has taken to rebuild highly specialised robots- the uncertainty of whether the Japanese bosses would agree to redo the plant and what that meant for 8000 jobs

Summary:
Summary

At 5 30 pm on the 12th April, Toyota security teams drove their golf carts around the massive plant at Prospecton in the South of Durban. As the rain came pouring down, they thought they were ready. There had been floods before in 2017 and Toyota had made provision for events like these. They had taken over the management of canals around the factory to ensure their multibillion robotic assembly line, filled with high precision electronics, would stay dry, even in the worst flooding.

15 minutes later, they knew they were in trouble. Upstream, there was panic as the Shongweni dam was about to overflow, so staff manning the sluice gates – opened the taps and a wall of water headed downstream directly towards the Toyota plant and the container store. Around the same time, the Umlazi river burst its banks.

The guard at the Toyota factory on his little golf cart – looked down one of the lanes and saw a wall of brown stuff – silt, sand and water coming straight towards him, and ran for his life. Soon every single part of the plant was under around 1/ 5 to 2metres of water. 4000 brand new vehicles were water logged and would later have to be scrapped. And all the robotics on the assembly line were filled with light brown silt. ( there is footage) The guard survived and there were no deaths.


Further information:
For the local Durban economy this was disastrous. Government values a huge multinational investor like Toyota and already they had weathered the July riots and chosen to stay. Toyota exports thousands of these Durban cars into Europe every year- And sells around 4000 Hilux’s into the local market every month.

So would the Japanese bigwigs at Toyota, call it a day or would they reinvest? The last few weeks six Japanese engineers have been assessing the damage with their local counterparts. Recently a decision was made. Toyota would stay and invest billions to get their plant back up and running. And work there is commencing at a cracking pace. But imagine this. Every single part in the assembly line has to be assessed to see if it can stay or must be replaced.

The 4000 scrapped vehicles are just a drop in the ocean in terms of losses. Because no cars have come off the assembly line since the 12th April. What they have lost in terms of exports and local production is 45 000 vehicles that would have been built in this time had it not been for the floods.

Carte Blanche speaks to the engineers, the guards, the CEO and the people that have saved 8000 crucial jobs down in the South Durban basin.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT
TOYOTA- MOTORING ON: TX SUNDAY 3RD JULY 2022 FACT CHECKED

Voice over One
Its endured a pandemic, massive social unrest, shipping delays and supply shortages,
But the wheels at Toyota’s Durban factory just kept on turning

Up sound

Across these 87 hectares – the size of 210 soccer fields, some of South Africa’s favourite cars are manufactured – then sold here, and in 74 different countries around the world

Up sound

8000 direct jobs – and thousands more across the whole value chain- this plant is a significant contributor to the KZN economy.

Up sound

And what goes wrong here- lands on the shoulders of executive Vice president Nigel Ward

Nigel
Howzit guys how are we doing?

And as far as he was concerned, 2022 was going to be the year everything would keep going right

Nigel
We were working 18 hours a day, that is two shifts, six days a week and every 90 seconds you see a Hilux come off

Voice over Two
With Nigel Ward directing operations from the factory floor, and having weathered two years of crises – CEO Andrew Kirby was looking forward to a brighter 2022

Andrew
When we came into 2022 we were hopeful that we will be able to start recovering, until of course the big rains in early April.

Voice over Three
On the 11th and 12th April a cut off low pressure system dumped around a third of KZN’s annual rainfall - over the Durban area.

Up sound Rain

Managers were on high alert -but hopeful that canals and other measures, put in place in the 2017 floods, would keep their plant dry.

Andrew
At 5:30 in the morning they sent us photos, no flooding, no damage at all on our site, so we were very pleased our activity had worked – but our relief was short lived.

Shongweni dam wall overflow

Voice over four
But upstream – Shongweni dam was overflowing, and two of its fuse gates tipped to avoid catastrophic failure to the entire dam- sending a biblical tide down the Umlazi river

Up sound water overflow

Voice over Five
Jan Els was already on site, he was the man sending the photo’s to Andrew Kirby

Jan Els
Then all of a sudden things went bad very quickly – I got a call to go to contractors gate-
when I arrived there I knew we were in deep trouble – there was a river of water and mud streaming into the plant, the car park was already flooded, there were cars already drifting but the water kept rising at an extremely rapid rate

Andrew Kirby
That surge of water then breached the banks of the Umlazi river, crashed through the empty container yard and flooded the whole South Basin, so between 5 30 and 6 20 am, suddenly we had about 1.5 meters of muddy water over our entire 87 hectare site
Masa
Wait Andrew from 5 30 clear?
Andrew
Nothing
Masa
06 20?
Andrew
1.5 meters under mud

Up sound squelch, squelch

Voice over six
Jan Els was about to have a very long, very wet day.

Jan
My personal thoughts at that stage was I am not sure how we are going to survive – are we ever going to be able to get this up and going again?

Voice over seven
First priority was to shut down power to avoid electrocutions


Jan
We were walking in mud and water this deep. The cars on hangers as they were coming down the hangers the cars- were flooded in mud. The pits
were flooded in mud. We had parts drifting everywhere, empty boxes, fallen part racks -it was just chaos

Voice over eight
Nigel finally managed to get to work the following morning – and the only place where he could find a cell phone signal was on the roof of the administration building

Nigel
Got here very early in the morning on the 13th and to be honest with you I wanted to cry.
We had no electricity no water although that sounds bizarre, and no communications
Masa
What were you seeing Nigel?
Nigel
Just mud it was almost an eerie feeling -everywhere was quiet. The N2 highway was closed, it had containers littered all over it – at that stage I couldn’t determine the damage on our site and l just thought whoa we have a job ahead of us!

Voice over nine
Staff knew their jobs were on the line – and managers like Larry Mchunu had to calm them down

Larry Mchunu
People were phoning us and asking what is happening – just to calm those nerves was one of our challenges

Link
So considering all the damage was it worth saving? And that was a decision that was going to be made in Japan

Voice over ten
Andrew sent Akio Toyoda – the president of the global company, the bad news via video message

Andrew
Nobody ever asked why did it happen, or could it have been prevented they just said how can we help?
Masa
Now I know you may not wish to reveal the exact figures but I am guessing it must be in the billions?
Andrew
We are very fortunate- TMC was able to give us eye watering level of support from a cash flow point of view. Uh- it’s in the tens of billions


Voice over eleven
And so began a massive damage assessment and clean up, but more than 4000 brand new vehicles had to be crushed -to ensure future quality

Andrew
But the loss of those vehicles was relatively small because we probably going to lose 80 000 vehicles production wise because of this length of shut down.

Voice over twelve
It’s been more than 80 days of rebuilding, directed from this command centre full of white boards and charts.

Across the plant Japanese engineers are having stand up meetings with their South African colleagues – and Masachi Asekura – Toyota’s top global risk manager, is here too

Masachi Asekura
This is the most comprehensive damage to any of our global production facilities

Voice over thirteen
Even worse he says than the Tsunami that hit Japan in 2011

Masachi Asekura
Yes, the tsunami is a limited section but here is all -whole facilities!

Voice over fourteen
The water was one thing – but it was the mud that dried to a fine powder, that almost defeated them

Andrew
We ended up with 77 generators on site, we had ten 20 000 water tankers cycling 4 times per day delivering water to us and the neighboring communities, – we had honeysuckers on site- those big pits - we had to pump 21 million liters out of the pit just to get the mud out, then we had to bring fresh water in to high pressure clean it, so it was a long process, and as the days unfolded we uncovered more and more damage

Voice over fifteen
And with their high tech robots covered in mud - and 120 000 parts on order that could take around six months to arrive – they had to make a plan

Andrew
So we have started the process of taking those control panels apart, one by one. With a toothbrush distilled water- cleaning it recleaning it, and going through a very slow tedious process
Masa
So like a literal toothbrush?
Andrew
Literally a toothbrush

Voice over sixteen
There is an energy and focus on this factory floor, and everyone is doing what they can -hoping to restart production at the end of July

Larry
Everybody was so motivated. Even the union -I mean I had shop stewards coming to me to say how can we help

Voice over Seventeen
And as KZN still reels from flood damage – at least here, the cogs of industry are beginning to move, and not a single job has been lost in the process

The END 08:02


PROMO ONE 11 seconds
After the recent catastrophic floods in KZN, a car manufacturer is cleaning, replacing, and rebuilding its massive plant – one part at a time

PROMO TWO
Masa
You here that?
KSH, KSH, KSH
Masa
That is the sound of production, contribution to our economy and jobs saved

Commentary
After KZN’s floods almost destroyed a leading car manufacturer – international engineers and South African teams are putting it back together – and they are almost there


PROMO THREE
In less than an hour on the 12th April the entire 87 hectare Toyota plant was covered in water and mud

Jan
my personal thoughts at that stage was I am not sure how we are going to survive – are we ever going to be able to get this up and going again

Commentary
Now it’s a long steady haul to get the cogs of their business moving again
